eyebrow: Quantum Error Correction & Fault Tolerance · Chapter 7
subtitle: Lesson 28 · Fault-Tolerant Computing

eyebrow: Error correction alone isn't the whole job

steps.label: A QEC code tells you how to fix an error after it occurs
steps.sub: Every gate, measurement, and correction round is itself a physical operation that can go wrong

steps.label: It doesn't guarantee the fixing process won't introduce new errors
steps.sub: Faster than you can catch them

steps.label: Fault tolerance is a genuinely different property
steps.sub: From 'the code has a high enough distance'

eyebrow: The precise definition, and fault-tolerant gadgets

steps.label: One faulty gate, ancilla, or measurement must never cascade
steps.sub: Into a logical error the code can no longer correct

steps.label: A single fault should cause, at worst, one correctable error
steps.sub: Never an uncontrolled spread that overwhelms the code

steps.label: Gadgets: sub-circuits engineered for single-fault containment
steps.sub: Transversal gates are the easy case — no qubit touches another during the gate

steps.label: Not every needed gate can be made transversal
steps.sub: Setting up the next lesson's magic-state distillation

eyebrow: The error-correction procedure itself must be fault-tolerant too

steps.label: Syndrome-extraction circuits are real gates and measurements
steps.sub: Subject to the exact same faults as everything else

steps.label: A naive ancilla circuit could spread an error across data qubits
steps.sub: During the very process meant to detect and fix errors — self-defeating

steps.label: Fault-tolerant extraction needs specially verified ancilla states
steps.sub: Real architectures spend serious engineering effort here, not just on the base code

subtitle: The one gate transversal tricks can't cheaply provide, and the expensive machinery built to supply it anyway.
